free_tier.stated: Basic plan on RapidAPI: 500 requests a month as a hard limit, 3 requests a second, and 10,240 MB a month of bandwidth, then USD 0.001 per MB.
free_tier.notes: Over the quota the API answers HTTP 429. The same station and point history is in the keyless bulk files (data-apis/meteostat).

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

egress.terms: 10,240 MB a month of bandwidth on the Basic plan, then USD 0.001 per MB

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at meteostat.p.rapidapi.com with the X-RapidAPI-Key header or the rapidapi-key query parameter; JSON answers
tooling: any HTTP client; the RapidAPI key goes in the X-RapidAPI-Key header
chaining: A keyed point-history API for small lookups; anything larger reads the keyless bulk files instead.

limits.value: 10,240 MB a month of bandwidth, then USD 0.001 per MB

binding_note: 500 requests a month is about 16 a day over 30 days, so the monthly hard limit binds long before 3 a second or the bandwidth allowance.

identity_cost.detail: A RapidAPI account (username, email and password, or a GitHub or Google sign-up) and a subscription to the Basic plan. Rapid's terms place a USD 0.50 hold on the card for freemium plans; whether subscribing to this hard-limited Basic plan asks for a card is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: A call with no RapidAPI key answers HTTP 401.
confidence_note: Quota, rate and bandwidth are read from the RapidAPI pricing page and the Meteostat API docs; a call with no key answered HTTP 401, so the Basic plan was not exercised.
